title: Harden admin journeys: RBACv2 threat vectors, SAML assertion audit & pen-test remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood recently onboarded RBAC v2 and consolidated SSO/SAML flows for admin paths. A third-party penetration test in Dec 2024 highlighted 6 medium/high findings across admin session elevation, assertion replay, incomplete audit lineage, and ambiguous fallback rules for legacy admin endpoints. This ticket coordinates threat-model follow-ups, concrete code & infra remediations, and post-deploy verification steps for admin journeys and audit pipelines.

Goals:
- Produce a prioritized, implementable remediation backlog tying each pen-test finding to a code change, infra config, or operational runbook.
- Ensure SAML assertion handling is fully auditable (request ID, issuer, subject, assertion hash) and retained in immutable audit logs with tamper-evidence.
- Harden RBACv2 evaluation for admin actions: remove legacy "admin:override" bypasses, enforce least-privilege defaults, and add telemetry for policy mismatches.
- Add canary + gradual rollout plan with automatic rollback if audit telemetry/regressions are detected.

Non-goals:
- Re-architecting entire auth stack. Focus is limited to admin-facing flows and immediate audit surface.

Scope & Deliverables:
1) Threat-model updates and acceptance criteria (security+eng): add specific attack trees for assertion replay, admin session takeover, and emergency admin escalation. Deliverable: updated threat-model doc (Confluence link below) and a short checklist for reviewers.
2) SAML assertion logging: augment assertion processing to emit structured events including assertion_id, issuer, subject, audience, assertion_hash, validation_result, and handling_path (primary|fallback). Deliverable: schema PR + log-forwarding mapping for SIEM.
3) Audit log immutability: add HMAC batch-signing for daily audit blobs stored in audit-bucket; track rotation keys in KMS and surface verification tooling. Deliverable: infra IaC change + verification script.
4) RBACv2 policy hardening: remove legacy "admin:override" wildcard bindings in critical services, convert emergency roles to time-limited grants, and introduce deny rules precedence for destructive APIs. Deliverable: policy migration PRs and a migration runbook.
5) Pen-test remediation code: address three high findings (assertion replay window, session fixation on admin proxy, missing MFA gating for critical calls). Deliverable: code PRs with test coverage.
6) Observability & SLOs: add dashboards for admin auth failures, assertion rejection rate, policy-mismatch rate, and a weekly audit pipeline verification job. Deliverable: Grafana dashboard + alerts.

Design & Implementation Notes / Trade-offs:
- Assertion payload redaction: we will log assertion metadata and hashes rather than full assertions to limit PII exposure. This trades full forensic reconstruction for lower exposure; we will retain encrypted raw assertions in a restricted KMS-encrypted store for 90 days as a compromise.
- HMAC vs. append-only store: implementing an append-only ledger would be ideal but higher effort. We choose daily HMAC-signed blobs with key rotation as a pragmatic intermediate step; we will revisit ledger if compliance requires it.
- Time-limited emergency grants: will be enforced via a new grants service that issues expiring tokens (TTL <= 1h). This requires small infra addition but reduces long-lived privileged tokens.

Open Implementation Tasks (owner & ETA):
- Finalize logging schema and map to SIEM (Marcus) — ETA 2025-03-03
- RBAC policy migration PRs across 6 services (InfraTeam + Marcus) — ETA 2025-03-10
- Emergency grant service RFC and initial prototype (Sana Rao) — ETA 2025-03-07
- Session fixation fix in admin-proxy + unit tests (Eng: ProxyTeam) — ETA 2025-03-05
- HMAC key rotation automation and KMS integration (InfraOps) — ETA 2025-03-12

Acceptance Criteria / Definition of Done:
- All high-severity pen-test findings marked closed in the vendor ticketing system with reproducible verification steps.
- Structured assertion events appear in SIEM within 60s of processing and follow the agreed schema.
- Audit blobs weekly verification job passes for 4 consecutive weeks.
- RBAC-related test coverage for critical paths added (>=80% branch on policy eval).
- Security team signs off on the threat-model update and remediation runbook.

Rollout Plan:
- Canary: deploy assertion-logging and policy changes to staging and a single low-impact customer tenant for 48h. Monitor alerts.
- Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic over 72h if no P0 alerts. Automated rollback if policy-mismatch rate or assertion rejections exceed thresholds.

PRs / Artifacts / Links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/admin-rbacv2-threatmodel
- Auth service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/1437
- Infra audit-signing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/88
- QA test plan: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example
- Pen-test report excerpt (vendor): https://internal-dashboard.redwood.ai/pen-test/2024-dec/summary

Risks & Contingencies:
- False positive spike: tightened assertion validation could surface false positives for legacy integrations. Contingency: add tenant-specific compatibility mode and migration guide.
- KMS limits / key rotation lag: ensure rotation is infra-backed with retries; if KMS throttling occurs, fallback to locally cached verification keys for up to 24h.

Notes for reviewers:
- Reviewers should focus on whether the logging schema provides sufficient forensic value without leaking assertion contents.
- Verify policy migration plan covers all admin routes (list attached in Confluence).
- Check that emergency grant TTL and audit hooks are present in the proposed implementation.
